**ID:** Ud 6.2 (PTS Ud 64)

**Title (Pali):** Sattajaṭila Sutta

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sattajaṭila Sutta* (Ud 6.2, PTS Ud 64) is the second discourse of the sixth chapter of the *Udāna* [Catalog]. The sutta addresses the problem of discerning another person's true character and spiritual attainments. In the narrative setting, King Pasenadi of Kosala sends out spies disguised as ascetics belonging to five different sectarian orders; when the king encounters the Buddha, the Buddha explains that an individual's moral integrity and whether they are an arahant cannot be ascertained on superficial observation, but requires prolonged association, close interaction, and wise attention [Evans, Doubting the Kālama-Sutta].

Full parallels to the discourse are found in the *Kosala Saṁyutta* of the *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 3.11, also titled *Sattajaṭilasutta*) and two Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* translations (SĀ 1148 and SĀ² 71). Passage-level verse parallels also occur in the *Satkāravarga* of the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 13) and its respective Chinese and Tibetan translations (T 212, T 213, Uv Kg 13).
